LESSON: READING SYLLABLES (JA-JU, LA-LU)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.2: Reading syllables (ja-ju, la-lu)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading syllables (ja-ju, la-lu), part of Reading in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do you think we learn to read syllables?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading syllables (ja-ju, la-lu) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner demonstrates hard work while practising to read syllables.

• Unity: The learner cooperates with peers as they practice reading syllables collaboratively.

Core competencies:

• Communication and collaboration: The learner articulates correctly sounds and blends them to form syllables with peers.

• Learning to learn: The learner persists in joining sounds to form syllables.

Values:

• Responsibility: The learner demonstrates hard work while practising to read syllables.

• Unity: The learner cooperates with peers as they practice reading syllables collaboratively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issue(
s) :

Effective communication: The learner practices to articulate syllables correctly as they chant syllables’ rhymes.

Chanting of rhymes on syllables links to singing of songs in Creative Activities.
